items.title: Tony Parenti and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-06-29
items.q: And you know something, Tony? That was the end of me seeing you for many years

ctx.x: Henry. I want to get that straight. There's so many out.

Well, Merritt and Henry. No, no. Well, Merritt was a trumpet player. There's only two trombone players. George and... George came, you know, later. But Henry was the... There was two trombones that Ernest Giordina used. And that was Eddie Edwards and Henry Brunas. They were two of the kings down there. It was... You might have heard about Tom Brown, but they could never play with Giordina's band, because Giordina would play stuff out unorthodox. You understand? He played more. Brown would only play what he knew,…

still play, you know. The old man, you're not a son. The old man, the son is dead, Pansy's dead. Pansy's dead. I went to his wake with Raymond Burke, you know. I never did know. I always see Raymond whenever I go down

items.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11
items.q: I play a lot with Tony up there.

ctx.x: Was Vic Lubowski Jewish? Did you know him? He played with Tony Periniot for years. He was a piano player.
I play a lot with Tony up there.
Ask him about Vic. There was another Zimmerman who played piano. Roy Zimmerman? No, Tony, I think this guy's name was. And Roy told me they're no relation.
